newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Puts main attraction in coffee, cocoa.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Puts main attraction in coffee, cocoa.

text.p: Players in coffee and cocoa options dabbled mostly in puts this week in an otherwise lethargic week for soft commodities, market makers said.
With cocoa futures flirting with highs some traders sold March 1,000 puts, taking the view that the market has bottomed out. Buyers of puts had a bearish stance and covered shorts.

Cocoa puts also featured in sidetrades with a spread on March 1,000 and 925 giving the buyer a long position at 925. Trade demand was brewing for March 1,000 calls and vols on out-the-money calls ticked up to 20 percent for any volume.
Put vols also traded at a slightly higher 15-16 percent.
"There is a skew towards the calls because the market believes there is more upside risk than downside," said one.
Cocoa futures were jolted out of a downtrend last week as speculators, taking their cue from New York, began to cover shorts. March firmed to 943 stg from last weeks low of 903.
But the rally was tagged as "technical" and traders said the market needed to take out 950 stg to look more appealing.

A recommended strategy for bulls was to sell the May 900 put and buy 1,050 call at roughly level money. The attraction of May is that it enables the buyer to have a clearer view of the Ivorian crop as more arrivals figures would have been received.
Little interest materialised for coffee options but a large open position on January $1,400 puts occupied traders' minds with only 20 days before the expiry.

Traders said the 1,400 lots open on the strike could be scene to serious delta hedging if the futures continued to hover around the trigger. "Until yesterday the (futures) range ($1,476-1,415) was quite secure," said one trader. "But with the way the market is going now, we may see some volatility nearer the expiry."
January futures broke through the crucial $1,400 and $1,360 support and traders said more losses were on the cards if the market closed below $1,360 on Thursday.
Bears were recommended to take on put spreads on January $1,400 and $1,300. These are trading at $50-55 premium compared with $68-70 for the outright January $1,400 put.

Volatilities were static with January around-the-money puts and calls at 28-29 percent and March at 24-25 percent. Coffee futures took a plunge on Wednesday on long liquidation ahead of November's Friday expiry, origin selling and sell-stops.
Mounting concerns over rising nearby physical supplies slashed Nov/Jan spread to level money on Thursday from a persistently-high level of over $100 in the past weeks.
